{{< include _elements-kit.qmd >}}

**Harmony** is the chords. **Tonality** is the key: which note feels like home, and whether the music is major, minor, or
something else.

## 1. Key signatures

The sharps or flats at the start of every line show the key. Each major key shares its signature with a **relative minor**,
three [half steps]{.nn} below it.

| Signature | Major key | Relative minor |
|---|---|---|
| none | C | A minor |
| 1♯ (F♯) | G | E minor |
| 2♯ (F♯ C♯) | D | B minor |
| 3♯ | A | F♯ minor |
| 1♭ (B♭) | F | D minor |
| 2♭ (B♭ E♭) | B♭ | G minor |
| 3♭ | E♭ | C minor |

**Major or minor?** The signature alone doesn't tell you. Look at the last note and chord (usually the tonic), and in
minor look for the raised 7th: music in A minor uses G♯, a sharp that is *not* in the key signature.

::: {.ax-pair}
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:C major
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
"C"E G c G|"F"A F "G"D B,|"C"C4|]
</script></div>

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:A minor: same signature, G♯ added
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:Am
"Am"A, C E C|"Dm"D F "E"E ^G,|"Am"A,4|]
</script></div>
:::

## 2. Major, minor, modal, atonal

| Tonality | What you hear |
|---|---|
| **Major** | in a major key; often sounds bright |
| **Minor** | in a minor key; often sounds darker or sadder |
| **Modal** | built on a **mode**, an older scale such as Dorian or Mixolydian; folk songs, medieval music, a lot of rock |
| **Pentatonic** | uses only five notes (C D E G A, the black keys of a piano); folk music round the world, blues, pop |
| **Atonal** | no key at all, no note that feels like home; some 20th-century classical music, film horror |

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Pentatonic: only C D E G A
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:C
E2 G2 A2 G2|E2 D2 C4|D2 E2 G2 A2|c2 A2 G4|]
</script></div>

## 3. Modulation

A **modulation** is a change of key in the middle of a piece. The most common moves are to the **dominant** (the key a
5th up, C to G) and to the **relative major or minor** (C major to A minor). In pop songs the last chorus often
modulates up a [half step]{.nn} or [whole step]{.nn} for a lift.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:A phrase in C, then the same phrase a whole step higher in D
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
"C"E G "F"A G|"G"F D "C"C2|"A7"z4|[K:D]"D"F A "G"B A|"A"G E "D"D2|]
</script></div>

## 4. Chords

A **triad** is a chord of three notes, each a 3rd apart: root, 3rd and 5th. Built on each note of the scale, triads are
numbered with Roman numerals: capitals for major, small letters for minor.

| | I | ii | iii | IV | V | vi | vii° |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| In C | C | Dm | Em | F | G | Am | B° |
| Name | tonic | supertonic | mediant | subdominant | dominant | submediant | leading note |

Adding another 3rd on top makes a **seventh chord** (G7 = G B D F). Adding more makes **extended chords** (9ths, 11ths,
13ths), common in jazz.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="70"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Triad, seventh, ninth on G
M:4/4
L:1/2
K:C
"G"[GBd]2|"G7"[GBdf]2|"G9"[GBdfa]2|]
</script></div>

For the rest of this: [Inversions](inversions.qmd), [Borrowed Chords](borrowed-chords.qmd).

## 5. Cadences

A **cadence** is the last two chords of a phrase, like punctuation. Two sound finished, two don't.

| Cadence | Chords | Sounds |
|---|---|---|
| [Authentic cadence]{.nn} | V → I | finished, a full stop |
| **Plagal** | IV → I | finished, softer: the "Amen" of hymns |
| [Half cadence]{.nn} | anything → V | unfinished, a comma or a question |
| [Deceptive cadence]{.nn} | V → vi (usually) | a surprise: you expect I and get a minor chord |

The names in this table follow the *British names* switch at the top of the page. The US and UK names differ here: the
British *perfect*, *imperfect* and *interrupted* are the American *authentic*, *half* and *deceptive*.

::: {.ax-pair}
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="80" data-style="hymn"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:V–I
M:4/4
L:1/2
K:C
"C"E "F"F|"G"D "C"C|]
</script></div>

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="80" data-style="hymn"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:IV–I
M:4/4
L:1/2
K:C
"C"E "G"D|"F"C "C"C|]
</script></div>
:::

::: {.ax-pair}
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="80" data-style="hymn"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:I–V
M:4/4
L:1/2
K:C
"C"E "F"F|"C"E "G"D|]
</script></div>

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="80" data-style="hymn"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:V–vi
M:4/4
L:1/2
K:C
"C"E "F"F|"G"D "Am"C|]
</script></div>
:::

**The Picardy third** (*Tierce de Picardie*): a piece in a minor key that ends on a **major** tonic chord instead of the
minor one you expect.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="76" data-style="hymn"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:D minor, ending on D major
M:4/4
L:1/2
K:Dm
"Dm"F "Gm"G|"A"E "D"^F|]
</script></div>

More: [Cadences](cadences.qmd), [Write an Ending](write-an-ending.qmd).
